scenes.title: Elpenor's Funeral
scenes.card: Back on Circe's island, the crew burns Elpenor's body and plants his oar on the grave, as promised.

subs.text: Book twelve.
The Cattle of the Sun.
Scene one.
Elpenor's Funeral.
The ship left Ocean's stream and came again to Aeaea, where young Dawn keeps her dancing-lawns;
they beached her on the sand and slept where the surf broke.
At dawn they fetched Elpenor's body from Circe's roof, and wept, and burned him with all his armor,
and heaped a mound above the ashes.
And on the crown of the mound they planted his shapely oar, as the dead man had asked.
Unflinching men —
you have gone down living to the house of Death;
twice-dying, when all others die once.
Eat now, and drink till nightfall;
at dawn you sail, and I myself will show you the road.

scenes.title: Circe Maps the Dangers
scenes.card: Circe privately describes each danger ahead and how to survive it, and warns Odysseus not to fight what cannot be fought.

subs.text: Scene two.
Circe Maps the Dangers.
Listen well, for the road ahead has teeth.
First the Sirens, who enchant every man that comes near them;
then a strait between two terrors, Scylla and Charybdis;
and beyond, Thrinacia, where the Sun keeps his cattle.
Knead sweet wax and stop your men's ears;
if you yourself must hear, let them bind you upright to the mast —
and bind you tighter when you beg.
Hug Scylla's cliff and row for your lives, for better six men lost than the whole ship swallowed by Charybdis.
And on Thrinacia touch nothing —
leave the Sun's herds unharmed, and you may yet come home.
But tell me truly, goddess —
when she strikes at my men, can I not stand to her with spear and sword and beat her off?
Stubborn man —
still spoiling for war and toil, still refusing to bow even to the gods!
She is not mortal;
she is deathless evil, terrible and wild, and not to be fought.
Against Scylla there is no defense but flight.
At dawn they went down to the swift ship, and the goddess sent a fair wind astern, filling the sail.

scenes.title: The Sirens' Song
scenes.card: Odysseus plugs his men's ears with wax and has them tie him to the mast, so he can hear the Sirens safely.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Sirens' Song.
Then the wind fell to a dead calm —
some god lulled the waves to sleep —
and ahead lay the island of the Sirens.
Ears to me, each man in turn —
this wax stays till we are long past that shore.
They bound him hand and foot, upright in the mast-step,
and beat the sea white beneath their oars past the flowering shore.
The Sirens promise total knowledge.
Odysseus struggles and signals to be released.
But Perimedes and Eurylochus rose and lashed him tighter still,
and the crew rowed until the song sank beneath the sound of the sea.

scenes.title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
scenes.card: Avoiding a deadly whirlpool, they row close to the opposite cliff, where the monster Scylla snatches six men from the ship.

subs.text: Scene four.
Between Scylla and Charybdis.
The crew hears Charybdis roar and sees spray rising from the whirlpool.
Row, friends —
we have been in worse and lived, and this too we shall remember.
Helmsman, hold her off that smoke and hug the cliff —
keep to the rock, or you kill us all.
Odysseus arms himself despite Circe's warning and searches the rock face.
Scylla's six heads strike, lifting six screaming men from the ship.
The survivors pass beyond both monsters while watching their companions die above them.

subs.text: Scene five.
The Island of the Sun.
The exhausted crew sees the cattle and sheep of Helios on Thrinacia.
Row on —
we do not land here.
Tiresias and Circe both warned me alike:
our worst harm waits on that island.
Call me merciless if you will, Eurylochus —
I would keep you alive.
The men swear to touch no livestock and land for one night.
A month of storm winds traps them while stores diminish.
Odysseus repeatedly reminds them of the oath.

scenes.card: While Odysseus sleeps, Eurylochus persuades the starving men to kill the sacred cattle; the Sun god demands revenge from Zeus.

subs.text: Scene six.
The Cattle Are Slaughtered.
When the last of Circe's stores was gone, Odysseus went up-island to pray the gods for a road home —
and they poured sweet sleep over his eyelids.
Eurylochus persuades the crew to sacrifice the best cattle rather than starve.
Eurylochus substitute oak leaves for barley and water for wine, kill the animals, and roast the meat.
The hides crawl and the meat bellows on the spits.
Lampetie tells Helios, who demands punishment from Zeus.

scenes.title: Zeus Destroys the Last Ship
scenes.card: Zeus strikes the ship with lightning and every man drowns; Odysseus alone clings to the wreck and drifts to Calypso's island.

subs.text: Scene seven.
Zeus Destroys the Last Ship.
What have you done —
you have slaughtered the Sun's own herds while I slept!
O father Zeus, you lulled me to my ruin.
This is doom, and no offering on earth will unmake it.
Six days they feasted on the finest of the cattle;
on the seventh the storm-wind fell, and they stepped the mast and stood out to open sea.
Zeus gathers a black cloud and strikes the mast with lightning.
The ship shatters and every crewman drowns.
Odysseus lashes keel and mast together.
Driven back to Charybdis, he hangs from the fig tree until the timbers reemerge, then drifts alone to Calypso.
